question.text: Mr. Rohit Bansal (Manager, Tapti Infrastructure AIF) is asked during DD: 'Why are manager track records critical in AIFs?' Per Ch 12, the CORRECT justification is:

answer.text: SEBI has mandated minimum 5-year track record for Manager SEBI registration.
Alternative investments depend critically on Manager skills and attributes, and empirical evidence suggests substantial upside to scheme returns based on the Manager's calibre.
Track record determines the fund's tax residency under Section 9A of the Income Tax Act.
Track record is the only factor SEBI considers during the PPM approval process.

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Chapter 12, 'alternative investments are based critically on the skills and attributes of the manager' and 'empirical evidence suggests a substantial upside to the return of a scheme based on the calibre of the manager'. The Trap: Option A invents a SEBI five-year track-record registration rule; option C wrongly links the manager's track record to Section 9A tax residency; option D treats track record as the only PPM input, which the workbook does not state. Note: The point being tested is the skill-dependence of alternative investments and its empirical effect on scheme returns - not any regulatory threshold.
